<!-- page:docs:reference/panel-report-schema.md path:/docs/reference/panel-report-schema -->
# Panel report schema

> Panel policy, slot identity, slot runs, panel findings, and the panel report.


A panel report records one ReviewFn panel run: several slots review the same frozen change, and their findings are combined by union. The panel contract lives in `@superfunctions/reviewfn-core` under `panel/`. Each document below has a JSON Schema (`panelPolicySchema`, `slotIdentitySchema`, `slotRunSchema`, `panelFindingSchema`, `panelReportSchema`, `lensOutputSchema`), TypeScript types, and a deterministic validator. The 0.1 `ReviewReport` v1 ([report schema](report-schema.md)) is unchanged. It is embedded as the panel's requirements report, and a 0.1 single-harness report validates exactly as before.

## Severity

Panel findings use the 0.1 `FindingSeverity`. Lens priorities map as P0 = `critical`, P1 = `high`, P2 = `medium`, P3 = `low`. A panel lens never emits `info`: the lens output schema excludes it, and the validator rejects it in panel findings with `REVIEWFN_PANEL_FINDING_INVALID`.

## Panel policy

`{ version: 1, slots, quorum: { stage1, stage2 }, requirementsSlot, maxConcurrentSlots?, incremental: "full" | "delta", profiles?, contextPairs?, contextExcludeGlobs? }`. `requirementsSlot` names a stage-1 or stage-2 slot, or is `null` to skip requirement extraction. `maxConcurrentSlots` is 1–8, and 2 when absent. `panelPolicyDigest(policy)` is the canonical SHA-256 of the validated policy with that default applied; the report records it as `panelPolicyDigest`. Loading the policy and repository tightening belong to the panel orchestrator.

A slot is `{ id, stage: 1 | 2 | "verifier", harness: { adapter, version, executable?, profile? }, inference: { provider, model, auth, credentialEnv? }, lens, budget: { timeoutMs, maxOutputBytes } }`. Slot IDs match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` and are unique. As in 0.1, the model `configured` defers to the harness default.

`profiles` maps profile names, which use the slot ID pattern, to harness profiles for the one profile-driven harness, the generic `cli` adapter (`@superfunctions/reviewfn-harness-cli`). A profile is `{ argv, promptVia: "stdin" | "file", outputVia: "file" | "stdout-last-json", envAllowlist, modelReport, capabilities: { structuredOutput, sandbox: "enforced-read-only" | "tree-verified-only" }, versionArgv? }`. A slot that names a `profile` must name one that `profiles` declares, and it must also name an `executable`. A slot may name an `executable` only together with a profile, only a slot whose `harness.adapter` is `cli` may name either, and a `cli` slot must name both. This pairing holds whatever the policy: the JSON Schema expresses it, so `panelStructureIssues` and `validatePanelReport` check it on the report's slots with or without a bound panel policy, and the panel refuses such a slot with `REVIEWFN_CONFIG_INVALID` before it runs. `argv` placeholders are the closed set `{promptFile}`, `{schemaFile}`, `{outputFile}`, `{workspace}` and `{model}`. Each is substituted only as a whole argument, so an element that holds a placeholder inside other text is invalid, and `versionArgv` takes none. `promptVia: "file"` requires `{promptFile}`, `outputVia: "file"` requires `{outputFile}`, and `capabilities.structuredOutput` requires `{schemaFile}`. `envAllowlist` holds unique environment variable names. `modelReport` is `none`, `json-path:<dotted path>` or `stderr-regex:<regex>`, and the regex must compile on its own and have exactly one capture group, counted from its source without ever running it. These checks report `REVIEWFN_PANEL_SCHEMA`. `validateHarnessProfile(value)` checks a single profile.

`contextPairs` and `contextExcludeGlobs` configure the `code-references` context adapter (see [configuration](configuration.md)). `contextPairs` is a list of `{ when, include }` rules: when a changed path matches the `when` glob, the files tracked at head that match any `include` glob (at least one) are paired with it, such as `{ "when": "migrations/**", "include": ["src/db/**"] }`. `contextExcludeGlobs` lists the globs the adapter never reads or reports; when absent, the defaults are `**/node_modules/**`, `**/dist/**`, `**/*.min.js`, `**/vendor/**` and the common lockfiles. Every policy glob uses a closed grammar: `*` matches within one path segment, `?` matches one character within a segment, a segment that is exactly `**` matches any number of segments, and every other character is literal. Braces, character classes, negation, escapes, `**` inside a segment, an absolute path and empty, `.` or `..` segments are refused with `REVIEWFN_GLOB_UNSUPPORTED`, both as a `validatePanelPolicy` issue and from `compileGlob` and the adapter constructor.

## Slot identity and runs

A slot's identity is the tuple (harness adapter, harness-reported version, provider, resolved model, auth mode, credential fingerprint). For a slot with a harness profile, the identity also records `harnessExecutable` and `harnessProfile`, which must equal the slot's and are part of the tuple. When the profile reports no model (`modelReport: "none"`), the identity records `modelVerified: false` and the configured model. Its key is then only (harness adapter, harness version, executable, profile), so runs of one executable and profile without a model report never count as distinct identities, whatever their configured provider, model, auth or credential. A harness that compared the raw reported model with the configured one and found them different records `modelMismatch: true` in the identity, even when `model`, redacted or cut to length, reads as the configured model. Such a run must be `void` with `model_mismatch`. A model reporter's raw `modelMismatch` verdict verifies the identity even without a model label, and `true` voids the run. A harness that reports `modelMismatch: false` (the raw model matched) records the configured model, so redacting or cutting its report never voids the run. `modelMismatch` needs a verified model and an explicitly configured model, and `model_mismatch` needs either a differing `model` or that flag. The fingerprint is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the credential value, or of the harness-reported account identity (`credentialFingerprint(value)`). The value itself is never recorded. The fingerprint is absent when neither was observed. `slotIdentityKey(identity)` compares identities. A run's harness adapter, provider and auth mode must equal its slot's. `harness.version` is the exact version the harness must report. A run that reports another version records that version truthfully, but it can never be `completed` or `collapsed`. This is a contract on whoever produces the report: such a run must be recorded as `failed` (or another terminal that does not count), and the validator rejects it otherwise, so a version drift cannot form a separate identity that escapes collapse.

Within one stage, slots with the same identity count once toward quorum. The run that counts is the first `completed` run of that identity in policy order. A later run of the same identity that would also complete is recorded as `collapsed`, so a `collapsed` run always follows a counted run of its identity in its stage. A run with `modelVerified: false` adds no identity beyond a counted run of its harness adapter, version, executable and profile: it is also collapsed into a counted verified run of those, wherever that run is in policy order (`slotCollapseTargets`). Runs that end any other way (`failed`, `canceled`, `quota_exhausted`, `timed_out`, `malformed` or `void`) neither count nor collapse: if the first slot of an identity fails, a later slot of that identity can still complete and count. A stage-2 slot may share a stage-1 identity, because stages have separate quorums. Collapse affects quorum only: a `collapsed` run succeeded with its own lens, its findings name it as their origin, and a collapsed verifier's verifications stand. Verifier slots collapse by identity in the same way, although they have no quorum.

A slot run is `{ slotId, identity, terminal, voidReasons, startedAt, finishedAt, outputArtifact?, outputDigest?, usage?, limitations? }`. `terminal` is `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, `quota_exhausted`, `timed_out`, `malformed`, `void` or `collapsed`. A `void` run lists at least one reason, and no other terminal lists any:

- `model_mismatch`: the resolved model differs from a configured model other than `configured`. This takes precedence over every other outcome: whenever the harness reports a resolved model that differs, the run is `void` and its reasons include `model_mismatch`, even if it also failed or timed out. When the harness reports no resolved model, `identity.model` records the configured model.
- `workspace_mutated`: the slot changed its checkout.
- `disallowed_tool_use`: the harness reported a forbidden tool.

`limitations` lists, without duplicates, what the run could not establish, without voiding it. `model_unverified`: the harness reported no model, so the configured model is unconfirmed. A run whose identity has `modelVerified: false` must list it, a run whose model is verified never lists it (the JSON Schema expresses both, so `panelStructureIssues` checks them too), and only a run of a slot with a harness profile may have that identity. When `validatePanelReport` is given the bound panel policy, the slot's profile also fixes these fields: a run of a `modelReport: "none"` profile must have `modelVerified: false` and list `model_unverified`, a run of a profile with a model reporter records `modelVerified: false` (and `model_unverified`) exactly when that reporter observed no model at preflight or in the run (preflight observes one only by setting `resolved.modelObserved: true`; a model it merely resolves from the configuration is not observed), so it never counts as a distinct identity, and a run of a `tree-verified-only` profile must list `sandbox_tree_verified_only`. `sandbox_tree_verified_only`: the harness enforces no tool restriction, and only the unchanged checkout was verified. The panel records the limitations of the slot's profile on every run of that slot, together with any limitation in this closed set that the harness reports as `observed.limitations`, except `model_unverified` on a run whose model is verified, which it drops.

Usage values (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `costUsd`) appear only when the harness observed them. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC with in-range fields. The validator also rejects dates that do not exist, such as February 30, and a run that finishes before it starts.

## Lens output

Lens slots return `{ findings, evidence, inspectedPaths, uninspected }`, which is the 0.1 harness output without requirements or assessments. The requirements slot keeps the full 0.1 harness schema. `HarnessInput.outputSchema` selects the structured-output schema for a run. The Codex adapter first compiles it as given with strict Ajv, then checks that it lies inside the provider strict subset that the lens and 0.1 harness schemas use (`unsupportedOutputSchema`). In that subset, the root is a `type: "object"` schema and is the only place for `$defs` or `definitions`. Object schemas have `type: "object"`, `properties`, `required` naming only those properties, and `additionalProperties: false`. Array schemas have `items`, `minItems` and `maxItems`. Scalar schemas have `type` (a list of scalar types may include `"null"`), `enum`, `const`, and string or number constraints. `anyOf` is a pure union and `$ref` points to a local `$defs` or `definitions` entry; neither takes another keyword. `description` and `title` may appear anywhere. Any other keyword or shape, such as `allOf`, `oneOf`, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `minProperties` or `$async`, fails the run before inference with a message naming it, distinct from the message for a schema that does not compile. Codex receives the provider-strict form (`strictProviderSchema`). Conversion is node-local: every property of an object schema is required, and a property gets a null alternative only when its own object schema does not require it. `const` and `enum` literals are copied verbatim. A property the caller schema requires keeps the values its own schema allows, including null when that schema allows it; a null the provider form added means the property is absent. The raw output must satisfy the provider-strict schema, or the caller schema as given, and no null is removed before this check. Nulls are dropped only afterwards, from the normalized result, which has empty requirements and assessments and must still be a valid 0.1 harness payload. Without `outputSchema`, Codex behaves as in 0.1.

## Panel findings

A panel finding is a 0.1 `Finding` plus the following fields:

- `origins: [{ slotId, lens }]`: at least one, and each a stage-1 or stage-2 slot with that lens whose run is `completed` or `collapsed`.
- `confidence`: 0–1. It is informational and never used for gating.
- `ruleIds`.
- `verification?: { verdict: "confirmed" | "refuted" | "inconclusive", slotId, evidenceIds, onBase: "present" | "absent" | "not_checked", reason }`.
- `disposition: "reported" | "dropped" | "suppressed"`, with `dispositionReason` and, for suppression, `suppressionReference`.

Verification comes from a `verifier` slot with a `completed` or `collapsed` run whose identity differs from every origin slot's identity, as collapse compares them (`sameSlotIdentity`). A confirmed or refuted verdict cites evidence. A dropped finding requires a refuted verification. A suppressed finding requires a `suppressionReference`, which is checked like a 0.1 waiver: it must be a verifiable reference (a literal excerpt or a valid line range) to an available, accepted source in the frozen context, and that source must be one of the policy's `sourceAuthority.waiverAuthorities`. Dropped and suppressed findings both require a `dispositionReason`. Dropped and suppressed findings stay in the report, so nothing disappears silently. Panel findings are lifecycle `new` until prior-finding provenance exists. Fingerprints are unique; agreement between slots is recorded in `origins`. The report records at most `policy.limits.maxFindings` panel findings, counting reported, dropped and suppressed findings alike; the panel orchestrator applies this bound to the slot union (see Union below).

## Panel report

The report is `{ schemaVersion: 1, kind: "reviewfn-panel", runId, createdAt, change, changeDetail?, contextManifestDigest?, panelPolicyDigest, slots, slotRuns, requirementsReport?, gateReceipts, evidence, findings, clusters, coverage, coverageReasons, verdict? }`.

- `contextManifestDigest` is the digest of the frozen context the run used. When a requirements report is present it must be equal to that report's digest, and it may be omitted. Source references are verified only against a supplied context with this digest (or the requirements report's). Without such a context they fail closed.
- `gateReceipts` are 0.1 test receipts from the trusted gates.
- `evidence` holds the 0.1 evidence items that panel findings and verifications cite. Each item is verified as in 0.1, and every check fails closed when the source control, context or artifact store it needs is not supplied:
  - Code anchors on findings and evidence follow the 0.1 commit rule (`anchorCommitChecker`). An anchor cites the reviewed head. It may cite the merge base only for a changed path that source control reports absent at head, and `changeDetail.since` only for a path the verified delta removed that is absent at head. One narrow allowance exists for on-base evidence: evidence cited by at least one verification whose `onBase` is `present` or `absent`, and by no finding and no verification whose `onBase` is `not_checked`, may anchor at the merge base on any path. Every anchor must then be confirmed by `sourceControl.verifyAnchor`. Without source control or with an empty `root`, source control is never called: only head anchors and on-base evidence pass the commit rule, and they still fail as unverifiable.
  - Diff evidence lies in the changed paths or the verified delta paths.
  - Source evidence cites a verifiable source in the frozen context.
  - Test evidence names exactly one gate receipt at the reviewed head.
  - Artifact evidence names the digest of a slot run's retained `outputArtifact`.
  - A reproduced finding needs a completed gate receipt at the reviewed head whose stdout and stderr artifacts match their digests in the artifact store.
- `clusters` are `{ id, findingFingerprints }`. A finding belongs to at most one cluster.
- `requirementsReport` comes from the run of the panel policy's `requirementsSlot`, as findings come from their origins. A `completed` or `collapsed` run must supply it, with execution `completed`. A run that ended any other way may supply a report that records its failure (execution other than `completed`), and no requirements report may exist without a run of that slot. The report's configuration names the slot's harness adapter and configured inference (provider, model, auth mode), and for a run that succeeded the slot's harness version. It must review the same change and change detail as the panel, and is validated with the 0.1 validator. Without it, the panel's own `changeDetail` is verified against its artifacts, and `changeDetail.since` is checked against head and merge base ancestry when source control can answer it, as in 0.1.
- Incomplete coverage states at least one reason.

`verdict` uses 0.1's derivation (`derivePanelVerdict`). It runs over the requirements report plus the reported panel findings; dropped and suppressed findings are excluded. Coverage is complete only if both the panel and the requirements report are complete. Without a requirements report no requirement was assessed, so the verdict is at most `needs_verification`. A requirements report whose run did not complete leaves the verdict absent, as in 0.1. Panel output stays advisory.

## Validation codes

`validatePanelReport(report, policy, { sourceControl?, root?, context?, artifacts?, panelPolicy? })` returns `{ valid, issues: [{ code, path, message }], verdict }`. `policy` is the 0.1 `ReviewPolicy` (blocking severities, source authority and limits). `panelPolicy` is the panel policy the run used: its digest must equal `panelPolicyDigest` and its slots the report's slots. It binds the requirements report to `requirementsSlot`, so without it a requirements report fails closed. Quorum and coverage derivation from slot runs belong to the panel orchestrator and are not checked here. `path` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, and the empty string `""` is the document root. Structural problems are reported alone. `validatePanelPolicy(policy)` checks a panel policy, including that `requirementsSlot` names a stage-1 or stage-2 slot. The codes form a closed set:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_SCHEMA` | The document does not match its JSON Schema, a timestamp is not a real time, the supplied panel policy is invalid or differs from the report's digest or slots, or a run contradicts its slot (harness adapter, provider or auth mode, a `completed` or `collapsed` run reporting another harness version, model mismatch not voided with `model_mismatch`, `model_mismatch` without a mismatch, finish before start). |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_SLOT_DUPLICATE` | A slot ID is declared twice, a slot has two runs, a second completed run of an identity in a stage is not collapsed, or a collapsed run has no earlier completed run of its identity in its stage. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_SLOT_UNKNOWN` | A run or verification names no such slot (`validatePanelPolicy` also reports an unknown `requirementsSlot`). |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_FINDING_INVALID` | `info` severity, more findings than `maxFindings`, a lifecycle other than `new`, a duplicate fingerprint or origin, missing, unknown or unverifiable evidence, unknown requirements, an unverified reproduction, an anchor whose commit the anchor rule above does not allow or that source control cannot confirm, or an invalid cluster. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_ORIGIN_UNKNOWN` | An origin is not a stage-1 or stage-2 slot with that lens whose run is `completed` or `collapsed`. Or the requirements report has no run of the bound panel policy's `requirementsSlot`, is absent although that run succeeded, or has an execution or configuration that contradicts that run and slot. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_VERIFICATION_INVALID` | The verifier is not a verifier slot with a `completed` or `collapsed` run, shares an origin slot's identity, or cites missing or unknown evidence. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_DISPOSITION_INVALID` | Dropped without a refuted verification, suppressed without a verifiable waiver-authority reference, a `suppressionReference` on a finding that is not suppressed, or dropped or suppressed without a reason. |
| `REVIEWFN_PANEL_VERDICT_MISMATCH` | `verdict` differs from the derived verdict. |
| `REVIEWFN_GLOB_UNSUPPORTED` | A `contextPairs` or `contextExcludeGlobs` glob of the panel policy is outside the closed glob grammar (`validatePanelPolicy` only). |

Errors from the 0.1 checks keep their 0.1 meaning: `REVIEWFN_CHANGE_DETAIL_MISMATCH` and `REVIEWFN_SINCE_NOT_ANCESTOR` keep their codes, and every other 0.1 error, including a requirements report for a different change, change detail or context, is `REVIEWFN_REPORT_INVALID`. Calendar validity of timestamps is a validator check beyond the JSON Schema pattern. `panelStructureIssues(kind, value)` is the structural TypeScript mirror of each JSON Schema. The tests check that it agrees with Ajv on every fixture and on systematic structural variants of each fixture.

## Panel orchestration

`PanelCoordinator` runs a panel and produces one panel report. The 0.1 `ReviewCoordinator` still serves the single-harness review. Both use the same code paths for preflight, change capture (`prepareReview`), harness output validation and redaction (`normalizeHarnessOutput`), 0.1 report assembly (`assembleReviewReport`), and artifacts.

- **Policy loading.** `loadPanelPolicy({ root, base, head, trustedFromBase })` reads `.reviewfn/panel.json`. The caller sets `trustedFromBase` (in CI, or with `--trusted-config-from-base`); the function does not detect CI itself. With it, the base revision's copy is required and trusted. A head copy that differs is applied with `applyRepositoryPanelPolicy`, and it may only tighten: raise quorums, add slots that each give a lens the pair does not have yet to a stage, harness and model pair the trusted policy already has (within that pair's budget), or lower budgets or `maxConcurrentSlots`. Trusted slots keep their IDs, fields and order; added slots follow them. Harness profiles come only from the trusted copy: the head copy may drop an unused profile, but a head copy that adds or changes a profile is a weakening. `contextPairs` and `contextExcludeGlobs` also come only from the trusted copy: a head copy that changes, adds or drops either is a weakening. Any other difference, such as a lower quorum, a removed slot, a changed model, lens, stage, `requirementsSlot` or `incremental`, or an added slot repeating a lens of its pair, is rejected with `REVIEWFN_PANEL_POLICY_WEAKENED`, which lists every weakening. Without `trustedFromBase`, the working-tree copy is read.
- **One preparation.** One trusted preflight covers the panel policy, the lens (`LensRegistry`; this release ships only `general`), harness and authentication of every stage-1 and stage-2 slot, the context adapters, execution and `since`. Verifier slots are not preflighted or run in this release (REV-16). The run then does one change capture, one context fetch and one test execution. Every slot receives the same frozen context and test receipts (the report's `gateReceipts`).
- **Harness versions.** A slot's `harness.version` is the exact version the harness must report. The harness is configured with its 0.1 adapter contract version: the run configuration's `harness.version` for the same adapter, otherwise `harnessContractVersions[adapter]`. A slot with another adapter and no entry there fails preflight with `REVIEWFN_PANEL_HARNESS_CONTRACT_UNKNOWN`. An adapter's `capabilities.version` is never used for this, because adapters such as Codex overwrite it with the executable's version during preflight. A run records the version the harness reported on its output, else the one preflight resolved, else the adapter's `capabilities.version`, else `unobserved`; the slot's pin is never recorded as a version.
- **Stages.** Stage-1 slots run first. Stage-2 slots then always run, whatever stage 1 found. Their prompt lists, as `stage1Findings` (possibly none), the findings of `completed` and `collapsed` stage-1 slots (collapsed as for the report) that pass the per-slot panel finding checks, merged by fingerprint, with the instruction to look for what stage 1 missed. Requirement links are neither checked nor passed on, and the `maxFindings` bound is not applied, so this list can differ from the findings the report records. Verifier slots are not run in this release; preflight warns `REVIEWFN_PANEL_VERIFIER_DEFERRED`.
- **Isolation.** Each slot runs in its own self-contained checkout of the head commit. Its own object store holds the head, merge-base and base commits, and `since` when the request sets it, with their trees (a depth-1 fetch by object ID from the run's repository), so a harness that sees only the checkout, such as one in a container, can read head, the merge base and the diff. It has no alternates, remote or other path outside it, no hooks, and attributes that keep the checked-out files byte-identical to the head blobs. After the slot finishes, the checkout's files are hashed through a run-owned Git directory of the repository's object format, into an index seeded from the head tree so submodule entries are kept. The slot's own `.git` is never consulted. The result is compared with the head tree. Directories the head lacks, `.git` entries in any letter case other than the checkout's own, content inside submodule paths, and entries that are not files, directories or symlinks (FIFOs, sockets, devices) are also detected. An observed difference, or a checkout the slot left in a state that cannot be compared, voids the slot with `workspace_mutated`, and the other slots' results stand. The comparison has its own bound (`comparisonTimeoutMs`, 60 seconds by default, capped at a quarter of `harnessTimeoutMs`), which each slot's harness timeout leaves before the stage deadline, so a slot that finishes in time always gets the whole bound. A comparison that does not finish within it makes the slot `timed_out`, never `workspace_mutated`, and a run cancellation during it makes the slot `canceled`. The head-tree listing is read as a stream, so an untouched checkout verifies as unchanged however large the repository. Every Git process of the checkouts runs one trusted absolute Git executable (`resolveTrustedExecutable`), never one looked up through `PATH` when it starts; so does reading the panel policy from a revision. Only Git's standard output counts toward the run's Git output limit (`maxGitOutputBytes`, 64 MiB by default); the warnings a checkout makes Git print, such as for embedded repositories, never stop or reclassify the comparison. A comparison stopped by that limit before a difference is observed makes the slot `failed` with that reason, never `workspace_mutated`; once the checkout's tree differs from head the slot is voided, even if the changed paths cannot be listed. Creating a checkout is bounded like a harness: it gets the time before the slot's harness deadline, and a provider that ignores its abort is abandoned after the abort grace, leaving the slot `timed_out` (or `canceled`). A run canceled while a checkout is created starts no harness. The checkout is removed after success, failure, timeout, cancellation and a harness that ignores abort, and a checkout created after its creation was abandoned is removed too. A harness that escapes its workspace on the host, or another local process changing a checkout during a run, is out of scope.
- **Budgets.** A slot's timeout is the smaller of `budget.timeoutMs` and the policy's `harnessTimeoutMs`. It starts once the slot's checkout exists. Its output limit is the smaller of `budget.maxOutputBytes` and `maxOutputBytes`. Both are passed to the harness. The limit applies to each output channel on its own, as harnesses enforce it on their streams: a structured payload (requirements, assessments, evidence, findings, inspected and uninspected scope), a transcript or serialized events larger than the limit gives `timed_out`, with a reason naming the channel, as does exceeding the timeout. Channels that are each within the limit are not added together. The panel stores at most the limit of the transcript (its first bytes) and of the events (the first whole events). Each stage is bounded by `harnessTimeoutMs`: each slot's harness timeout leaves the abort grace (`abortGraceMs`, 10 seconds by default, capped at a tenth of `harnessTimeoutMs`), the comparison bound, the comparison's abort grace and one more grace for cleanup before the stage deadline, so a harness or checkout creation that ignores abort and a comparison that ignores its bound still end by it. A slot that cannot start its harness with that time left, or is still queued, is `timed_out`. Removing a slot's checkout does not hold its place or use its stage's time: removals run in the background, and the run waits for them, and then removes its checkout directory, until the last stage's deadline (one abort grace after a cancellation). A removal or abandoned creation that has not finished by then is recorded as a coverage reason naming it, and is still attempted. Panel wall time is therefore bounded by `harnessTimeoutMs` times the number of stages, plus the verifier's budget once verifiers run (REV-16); preparation and storing artifacts are outside that bound. At most `maxConcurrentSlots` slots run at once. A harness abandoned after ignoring abort no longer holds a place: its slot ends, its checkout is removed and a queued slot may start, so its process, if it keeps running, is not counted against `maxConcurrentSlots`.
- **Slot outcomes.** Only a harness terminal (`completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, `quota_exhausted`, `timed_out`, `malformed`) is taken from the harness. A missing or unknown terminal, or `void` or `collapsed`, which only the panel decides, makes the run `malformed` with a reason and no findings. A served model other than the configured model voids the run with `model_mismatch`. This precedence applies to every run, including one that ended before its harness ran, whose model is the one preflight resolved. A reported forbidden tool voids the run with `disallowed_tool_use`. A run that would otherwise be `completed` is `failed` when its harness reports another version than the slot pins; other terminals, and `void`, are kept. Every run, whatever its terminal (including a slot canceled or timed out before it started, or whose checkout could not be created), is recorded with its reasons in the run result and in a retained output artifact (`panel-slot-output`, referenced by `outputArtifact` and bound by `outputDigest`) that holds its final terminal after collapse. If that artifact cannot be stored, the run has no `outputArtifact`, and the failure is among its reasons and the coverage reasons. A run's `finishedAt` is never before its `startedAt`, even when the clock steps back. Every run that does not count has at least one reason, even when its harness stated none. A failed slot is never retried or replaced by a fallback. Harnesses may report `observed: { harnessVersion?, model?, modelMismatch?, accountIdentity?, disallowedTools?, usage?, limitations? }` on their output. A run reads one copy of the request's panel policy, taken when `run()` or `preflight()` starts, so a later change to the caller's object never reaches it. A slot with a profile is configured with the slot's `executable`, its `profile` name and the trusted policy's profile, as `harness.profileDefinition`; a configuration file never sets these. For a profile without a model report, a reported model is ignored. Values they do not report are taken from preflight or configuration, and usage is never estimated.
- **Quorum.** Within a stage, the first completed run of an identity counts and later completed runs of that identity are `collapsed`. A stage with fewer counted runs than its quorum makes coverage incomplete with a reason starting `REVIEWFN_PANEL_QUORUM_UNMET`, so the verdict cannot be `ready`.
- **Union.** Each completed or collapsed slot's findings are validated alone against the panel contract. An invalid finding is excluded with a coverage reason that names its slot, so it cannot remove another slot's valid finding. An issue in a slot's run excludes only that slot's findings; it never excludes another slot's findings, in the report or in the stage-2 context. Every remaining finding enters the report, even when only one slot reported it, up to the policy's `maxFindings`; past that bound the lowest-severity findings are left out and coverage is incomplete with a reason saying how many. Findings with the same fingerprint merge: their origins, evidence and highest severity are kept (the fingerprint covers requirement links, so merged findings link the same requirements). A slot's `admittedFindings` counts the recorded findings it is an origin of, after the `maxFindings` bound. Agreement is recorded in `origins` and `confidence` (the share of contributing slots) and never filters a finding. Evidence IDs are prefixed with the slot ID. The requirements slot's findings also join the union, except `info` findings, which stay in its requirements report.
- **Coverage.** Coverage is incomplete when no slot completed, when a contributing slot reports scope it did not inspect, when changed paths (delta paths in delta mode) were inspected by no contributing slot, when a slot finding was excluded, when findings were left out by `maxFindings`, when a checkout or the run's checkout directory could not be removed or a slot output could not be stored, when the requirements report could not be built, and when the report itself fails validation, as well as for the 0.1 reasons (context, execution, failed tests, change detail) and cancellation.
- **Cancellation.** Cancellation is observed until `run()` returns. When it is observed after the slots ran but before the report is stored, the report is built again in canceled mode: coverage is incomplete with the reason `The panel run was canceled.`, and a completed requirements slot becomes `canceled`, so its requirements report records a canceled execution and no report built after the cancellation records a completed result. The shared 0.1 report path stores nothing further once it observes the cancellation; a requirements report it stored before then is superseded. The canceled-mode report names, in its coverage reasons and in the result's `supersededArtifacts`, every artifact the interrupted pass stored that it did not store again (slot outputs, the requirements report and its events, and an earlier panel report). An abort while the report is being stored makes the run store such a superseding report and reject with `REVIEWFN_CANCELED`, whose `details.reportArtifact` names the superseding report, `details.supersededReportArtifact` the earlier one and `details.supersededArtifacts` every superseded artifact.
- **Run identity.** The panel `runId` binds the change, context, review policy, configuration, panel policy, each slot's lens (ID, version and a digest of its instructions) and adapter contract version, the test receipts, the panel prompt version and `since`. The requirements report's `runId` binds the panel `runId`, the slot, the harness version it ran under and the digest of the prompt it was given.
- **Requirements.** The requirements slot uses the 0.1 prompt and schema over the full change, plus its lens. With `since`, its panel input also lists the delta (`since`, paths and hunks), including paths that exist only at `since`, because its report must account for every delta path. Everything in its panel input other than the lens instructions, including the stage-1 findings, is marked as untrusted data. Its 0.1 report is built by the shared 0.1 report path; its execution follows the slot's harness terminal, except that a run that does not count but whose harness completed records `canceled` for a canceled run and `failed` otherwise.
- **Delta mode.** With `incremental: "delta"` and `since`, lens slots receive the delta hunks as their primary scope and the full change and hunks as reference. Requirements are always assessed against the full change.
- **Report.** The panel report is validated with `validatePanelReport` against the run's frozen context, artifacts, source control and panel policy, and is stored as a `panel-report` artifact. If validation finds issues, the report is still stored, with coverage incomplete, the issues as coverage reasons, and the verdict re-derived. Panel output stays advisory.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/panel.md path:/docs/reference/panel -->
# Panel review CLI

> Run a review panel, its exit codes, harness adapters, outputs and report rendering.


A panel review runs several harness slots over one frozen change and combines their findings into one advisory panel report. The panel policy, slot identity, quorum and report contract are described in the [panel report schema](panel-report-schema.md). This page covers the CLI.

## Commands

```sh
reviewfn init --panel
reviewfn panel --base REF --head REF [--since SHA] [--issue KEY] [--pull-request N] [--panel FILE] [--output DIR] [--trusted-config-from-base] [--json]
reviewfn report --panel [--input FILE]
reviewfn publish --input .reviewfn/output/panel-report.json --repository OWNER/REPO --pull-request N --head SHA
```

- `reviewfn init --panel` writes `.reviewfn/panel.json` and refuses to overwrite an existing file. The template has a general stage-1 slot, which also extracts requirements, and a general stage-2 slot, both on the Codex harness. Each slot's `harness.version` is the exact version the harness reports, such as the output of `codex --version`. Update it to match the installed harness; a run that reports another version never counts.
- `reviewfn panel` loads `.reviewfn/config.json`, `.reviewfn/policy.json` and `.reviewfn/panel.json`. In GitHub Actions, or with `--trusted-config-from-base`, it reads them from the base revision, and a head copy of the panel policy may only tighten the base copy. It reviews a private snapshot of the repository at the head commit. `--since` names an earlier reviewed commit. Slots review only the change since that commit (a delta panel) when the panel policy sets `incremental: "delta"`; the `init --panel` template sets `"full"`, under which every slot reviews the whole change and `--since` only records the commit in the report. `--issue` selects the issue for context adapters. `--pull-request` binds the run to a pull request, as in 0.1. `--panel FILE` reads the panel policy from another repository-relative path.
- `reviewfn report --panel` re-renders a stored panel report (`.reviewfn/output/panel-report.json` by default) after checking its structure. Without `--panel`, it renders a 0.1 `report.json`.
- `reviewfn publish` accepts a panel report as well as a 0.1 report. A panel report publishes under the `panel` profile only, as one summary comment and one neutral `ReviewFn / panel` check. Publishing the same run again updates them; a canceled run is never published. The panel summary has its own comment marker and check ID, so a 0.1 report never replaces it, even under a profile named `panel`. Publication stays a separate, credentialed job.

## Outputs

The run writes `panel-report.json` and `panel-report.md` to the output directory (`.reviewfn/output` by default). Its evidence, including each slot's redacted output, the context manifest and the stored panel report, is kept in the content-addressed store under `.reviewfn/artifacts`, with the retention the policy sets. The two report copies have the same report retention (the smaller of the config and policy `reportDays`): each run expires old artifacts and copies, and idle stores need the scheduled cleanup described in [security](security.md). Add both directories to the repository's ignore rules. Several repositories or checkouts may share one absolute `--output`: each run replaces the pair there, and the copies' retention record, `.panel-report-copies`, lives in the output directory with them, so whichever repository cleans up next expires them correctly. Writes and cleanup of that directory take its `.panel-report.lock`; the [security](security.md) page describes what to do with a lock a crashed run left behind.

Without `--json`, the rendered Markdown is printed on stdout. With `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON line, printed only after the run's private snapshot is removed, `{"report":"<absolute path of panel-report.json>","runId":"<run ID>"}`, for scripting. Either output is printed only for exit 0, exit 2, and an exit 4 whose saved report records the cancellation, and only when the private snapshot was removed. Every other exit, including an exit 1 after the report was saved (retention cleanup failed or the private snapshot could not be removed), leaves stdout empty. Each error is one JSON object per line on stderr, `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "…", "details": … }`. A private snapshot that cannot be removed always adds a `REVIEWFN_SNAPSHOT_CLEANUP_FAILED` line whose `details.snapshot` names the directory to delete; it turns exit 0 or 2 into exit 1 and leaves exits 1, 3 and 4 unchanged.

## Exit codes

The exit codes form a closed set. The verdict never changes the exit code, because panel output is advisory.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The run completed and its coverage is complete. |
| 2 | The run completed with incomplete coverage, or a stage's quorum was not met. The report is written. |
| 3 | Preflight failed: invalid configuration or panel policy, a panel policy the head weakens, an unsupported or missing harness adapter, a `--base`, `--head` or `--since` ref that does not name a commit, a component's preflight refused the run, or an output directory whose `.panel-report.lock` is still held after about five seconds (`REVIEWFN_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_BUSY`, such as a lock a killed run left behind) or is a symlink (`REVIEWFN_ARTIFACT_UNSAFE`), or an `--output` directory that is the `.reviewfn/artifacts` directory itself (`REVIEWFN_ARTIFACT_UNSAFE`). No harness runs and no report is written. A cancellation during the wait for the lock ends it at once and exits 4. |
| 4 | The run was canceled (SIGINT or SIGTERM) before its report was saved, or its saved report records the cancellation. A failure while canceled before saving begins, including a preflight or setup step that the cancellation interrupted, also exits 4. A run that exits 4 leaves one of two results. Either nothing of the run is saved: no artifact is imported into `.reviewfn/artifacts` and no report copy is written (retention cleanup, which runs first, may still expire earlier copies whose retention has ended). Or the report records the cancellation: its evidence is imported and both copies are saved, unless saving them fails; `reviewfn publish` and the GitHub publisher refuse such a report as canceled. Saving imports the evidence and then writes the two copies. A cancellation that arrives once saving has begun does not stop it, and the run exits as if it had not been canceled: 0 or 2, or 1 if saving fails. |
| 1 | Any other error, such as an invalid argument (including a value flag given without a value or with an empty one, such as `--output=`), a private repository snapshot or run directory that cannot be created, an output directory that cannot be written or whose lock another run took after preflight (`REVIEWFN_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_BUSY`; neither copy is then written), a run whose evidence could not be imported (no copy is then written), a completed run whose retention cleanup failed (`REVIEWFN_RETENTION_CLEANUP_FAILED`), or a completed run whose private repository snapshot could not be removed. In the last two cases the report is saved, but stdout stays empty. |

## Harness adapters

A slot's `harness.adapter` is resolved through a fixed table to an installed package, and adapters are never loaded from arbitrary module paths. The intended model is that adapters are optional peer installs. In this release the Codex adapter, `@superfunctions/reviewfn-harness-codex`, ships as a direct dependency of the CLI. The `claude-code` and `cli` packages are not published yet; once they are, each resolves when it is installed next to the CLI, and until then a slot naming them fails with `REVIEWFN_HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED`:

| `harness.adapter` | Package | Export |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codex` | `@superfunctions/reviewfn-harness-codex` | `CodexHarnessAdapter` |
| `claude-code` | `@superfunctions/reviewfn-harness-claude-code` | `ClaudeCodeHarnessAdapter` |
| `cli` | `@superfunctions/reviewfn-harness-cli` | `CliHarnessAdapter` |

A `cli` slot runs any agent CLI that reads a prompt and writes JSON. It names its `executable` and a `profile` that the panel policy's `profiles` declares, and the profile sets the argv template, the prompt and output channels, the environment allowlist, the model reporting and the sandbox capability. No profile ships as a default. The package README gives unverified example profiles. A `cli` slot missing its profile or executable is invalid (`REVIEWFN_PANEL_SCHEMA`), and a `cli` slot never runs the configuration file's `harness.executable`. The `cli` adapter refuses pull-request review (`REVIEWFN_PR_AUTH_REQUIRED`), as `claude-code` does, and a refused slot's harness is never preflighted or run.

The CLI constructs each adapter once with `{ executable?, environment }`. The executable is passed only to the adapter that `config.harness` names. A slot whose adapter package is not installed fails preflight with `REVIEWFN_HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED`. An adapter outside the table fails with `REVIEWFN_HARNESS_UNSUPPORTED`. A package that does not export a matching adapter fails with `REVIEWFN_HARNESS_LOAD_FAILED`. For an adapter other than the configured harness, the adapter contract version is read from its capabilities before any preflight. Verifier slots are not run by this release, so their adapters are not loaded.

## Report rendering

The Markdown report shows:

- the run summary: run ID, reviewed head, base, coverage, verdict and finding counts;
- coverage limits;
- a table with each slot's stage, lens, harness, model (marked unverified when the harness reports none) and terminal state, with the reasons for a `void` run, for a `collapsed` run the slot whose identity it shares, and the run's limitations;
- the requirements summary, when the panel extracted requirements;
- reported findings, grouped by severity and then by file. Each finding shows its origins, its verification verdict, its on-base label (also present on base, new in this change, or not checked against base) and each piece of evidence it or its verification cites, with its kind, description and location (code anchor, source anchor, test receipt or artifact), so a finding without its own anchor can still be located;
- dropped and suppressed findings, with their reasons, in a collapsed section;
- the gate receipts.

`renderPanelMarkdownReport` in `@superfunctions/reviewfn-core` produces this rendering, and the GitHub summary uses the same text.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/report-schema.md path:/docs/reference/report-schema -->
# Report schema

> Execution, coverage, verdict, assessments, evidence, and findings.


A report records three independent axes:

- execution: `queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, or `superseded`;
- coverage: `complete` or `incomplete`, with reasons;
- verdict: `ready`, `changes_requested`, or `needs_verification`, absent unless execution is `completed`; a completed run without complete coverage or requirements is `needs_verification`.

Requirements contain immutable source anchors and exactly one assessment. Assessments distinguish `implemented`, `partial`, `missing`, `unverified`, and source-waived `not_applicable`. Evidence links to a context source, exact-head code anchor, diff, test receipt, or content-addressed artifact. An implemented assessment must include reviewed-head implementation evidence. Merge-base anchors can document deleted code but cannot alone establish implementation. An available source with no extracted requirements needs explicit source evidence with a nonblank `sourceExclusionReason`; ordinary citations do not establish exclusion.

Findings carry a fingerprint, severity, concrete trigger/impact/direction, reproduced-versus-inferred basis, requirement links and lifecycle. Model confidence never substitutes for evidence validity. Fingerprints use path, optional symbol and finding semantics, excluding revision and line coordinates. They are correlation hints, not proof of historical lifecycle. Version 0.1 receives no prior-finding provenance, so only `new` findings validate; every historical lifecycle remains unproven. Ambiguous duplicate fingerprints fail validation; distinguish actual symbols or defect semantics before correlation.

`contextManifestDigest` identifies the normalized snapshot bytes and `contextManifestArtifact` names the corresponding content-addressed stored artifact. Test receipts contain exact argv, commit, timing, exit status, stdout/stderr digests and limitations; they do not claim a retrievable log artifact unless one was actually persisted.

`changeDetail` is optional and additive; a report without it validates as before. When present, `hunksArtifact` names a content-addressed `change-hunks` artifact whose SHA-256 is `hunksDigest`. The artifact is a `ChangeHunks` v1 document, `{ version: 1, baseCommit, headCommit, files: [{ path, previousPath?, status, hunks: [{ oldStart, oldLines, newStart, newLines }] }] }`, parsed from `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --find-renames -U0 <mergeBase> <head>`. `status` is `added`, `modified`, `deleted`, `renamed` or `binary`. Binary files have no hunks, and the report lists them as limitations because they cannot carry line-level evidence. Diffs larger than the policy's `maxOutputBytes` are not parsed: the report omits `changeDetail` and records incomplete coverage with the reason. The same holds when the artifact store refuses the hunks artifact. Combined diffs, word diffs and external diff drivers are rejected (`REVIEWFN_DIFF_UNSUPPORTED`).

An incremental run sets `since` to the previously reviewed head, a full 40- or 64-hex commit. `since` must be an ancestor of the head and a descendant of, or equal to, the merge base. Otherwise the run fails before review with `REVIEWFN_SINCE_NOT_ANCESTOR`, and it never falls back to a full review. The report then also records `deltaHunksArtifact` and `deltaHunksDigest` for `since..head`, plus `deltaPaths`, the delta's changed paths. Like every changed path, each delta path must be inspected or explicitly uninspected. A delta path that the verified delta removes but the full change never lists (a file added after the merge base and deleted by a later push) is inspected at `since`; code and finding anchors may cite `since` only for such removed paths. The validator recomputes both digests from the stored artifacts and checks their commit ranges and paths against the change. Any mismatch fails with `REVIEWFN_CHANGE_DETAIL_MISMATCH`.

The validator rejects duplicate identifiers, unknown requirements/evidence/sources, stale commit anchors, invalid line ranges, unjustified exclusions, over-limit findings, incomplete-ready reports and any verdict inconsistent with deterministic policy.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/security.md path:/docs/reference/security -->
# Security model

> Trust boundaries, Docker containment, credentials, and retention.


The trusted boundary contains the pinned installation, base-revision policy, context collector, coordinator and separate publisher. Repository files, retrieved text, test output and model output are untrusted.

The CLI clones the committed target into an owned independent checkout. Mutable tracked and untracked caller files are excluded. The source adapter independently rejects dirty review roots. Configuration is loaded from the immutable base revision in CI; a PR cannot select its own executable, commands or limits. Global execution configuration must be controlled by the runner administrator.

Tests require Docker; there is no host-execution fallback. The pinned Node 22 image runs with no network, no capabilities, no privilege escalation, a read-only root, an unprivileged UID, 1 CPU, 512 MiB memory, 128 PIDs, a 256 MiB workspace and 64 MiB temporary filesystem. Input archives are bounded at 256 MiB. Only the committed archive is mounted read-only; no home directory, credentials, source checkout, Docker socket or host output directory is available to tests. The entire container is removed on every terminal path, including successful parents with detached descendants. Commands share a batch deadline and have bounded output. Dependencies must be present in the trusted image or committed input; commands cannot install them over the network.

PR inference requires action-proxy authentication and the trusted `reviewfn-codex:0.154.0` image. Build its packaged Dockerfile before running. The review checkout is read-only; only a fresh owned result directory is writable on the host. CPU, memory, PID, temporary disk, runtime and output limits also apply to inference. The proxy endpoint provides inference access only; it must not embed a raw provider credential. The container has outbound networking for this proxy and receives no publication token or host home directory. Restrict its egress at the runner/network layer where repository confidentiality requires a single allowed destination.

Codex disables project-document loading and user config. Changes to `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `.codex/`, `.agents/`, or `.claude/` fail before inference. API-key and ChatGPT modes are available only for trusted local reviews without a PR identity. Access-token and workload-identity modes currently fail explicit compatibility preflight. There is no automatic authentication fallback.

The review CLI refuses a process environment containing `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Publication uses a separate trusted job and a retained report, without running repository code or inference. Use a per-repository/PR/profile concurrency group for cross-run serialization. Head checks occur after comment discovery and before comment/check writes. GitHub does not provide a transaction spanning head changes and comment creation; a race after a check is reported stale, and every comment names its reviewed SHA. Checks remain neutral.

Artifact filenames and metadata identities are validated. Reads and writes reject target and parent symlinks, apart from known root-owned macOS system aliases. Atomic private output writes occur outside the untrusted execution boundary. Retention validates matching metadata IDs before deletion. Tests retain redacted logs; transcripts require `retainTranscript: true`; events and all harness output are redacted using both detected secrets and the explicitly configured credential value. The CLI applies retention cleanup when saving a new run. Operators must schedule `new FileArtifactStore(artifactsDirectory, outputDirectory).deleteExpired()` for idle stores; the optional second directory includes CLI report.json/report.md copies in expiry cleanup. `reviewfn panel` keeps its evidence in `.reviewfn/artifacts` and its panel-report.json/panel-report.md copies under the same report retention (the smaller of the config and policy `reportDays`); schedule `new FileArtifactStore(".reviewfn/artifacts", outputDirectory, PANEL_REPORT_COPY_NAMES).deleteExpired()` for each panel output directory (any artifacts directory cleans a panel output directory correctly, since the retention record is kept in it). The panel copies' retention record, `.panel-report-copies`, lives in the output directory next to the copies, so it always describes the pair actually there, whichever repository, checkout, copied artifacts directory or spelling of the path wrote it, and deleting the directory deletes the record with it. Every panel copy write, its rollback and every cleanup of the directory hold `<output>/.panel-report.lock`, taken inside the artifacts directory's .retention.lock (always in that order) and created exclusively without following symlinks; a symlinked or non-regular lock is refused, and a lock still held after about five seconds fails the write or cleanup with REVIEWFN_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_BUSY, naming the file. Like .retention.lock, it records PID, hostname and acquisition time; remove it only after confirming that process is dead on the recorded host. `reviewfn panel` checks the lock in preflight, waiting the same bounded time, and exits 3 before any harness runs while it is still held. Several repositories may therefore share one absolute `--output`: each run replaces the pair, and the last writer's pair is the one retained. The panel copies are staged and replaced as a pair under that lock: a failed write restores the previous pair and record and removes its staged files. Only a crash between the two renames, or a failed restore of the previous Markdown copy, can leave a mixed pair, and the record then keeps covering both the old and the new bytes so they still expire. Under the lock no copy write is in flight, so cleanup also removes any staged panel copy (`.reviewfn-copy.panel-report.<uuid>.json` or `.md`) a crashed write left in the directory; staged copies of another copy set are left to that set's own lock and cleanup. Shared content keeps the longest active expiration, including imports from run workspaces. Store mutations serialize through .retention.lock; after a crashed writer, the lock records PID, hostname, and acquisition time. Remove it only after confirming the owning process is dead on the recorded host; never reclaim an ambiguous or active owner automatically. Exports changed outside ReviewFn are preserved with a cleanup error rather than deleted. Failed 0.1 report copy writes retain expiry coverage for both old and proposed bytes; cleanup also removes content-addressed data orphaned before its metadata commit. The CLI saves the new review outputs but exits nonzero with REVIEWFN_RETENTION_CLEANUP_FAILED when cleanup reports errors.

Public forks never receive repository secrets. A proxy and isolated runner must be deliberately provisioned before enabling reviews. The publisher must download only the artifact from its trusted review job and verify PR/head/profile against event metadata. Never execute a PR-owned workflow, package or image with publication credentials.

Linked Linear document URLs must share the server-returned issue URL workspace, and returned canonical document URLs are rechecked before their content enters review context. Issue-attached document records inherit their verified issue association. Missing optional Markdown globs are accepted as empty selections; use an exact file path when absence must make context incomplete.

Host snapshot checkout, source capture, and test archive preparation use credential-free Git environments with system/global configuration disabled; checkout also disables templates, hooks, and global attributes. Reproduced findings require a completed reviewed-head test receipt and retained logs whose digests verify. Requirement text alone cannot substantiate a defect finding.

Deleted changed paths may use verified merge-base code anchors only when the source adapter proves the path is absent from the head. Existing paths still require head-commit anchors.


Native tool lookup on Windows resolves `.exe` binaries and rejects repository-owned paths; shell-dependent `.cmd`/`.bat` wrappers are not supported. POSIX world-write and execute-bit checks apply only on POSIX. Windows operators must provision PATH directories with trusted ACLs: Node's `stat.mode` does not validate Windows ACL ownership. Native Windows executable-name handling has regression-test coverage by simulating `process.platform` on POSIX. The full consumer and Docker gates remain verified on POSIX, not Windows end to end.

Normalized Codex telemetry is capped at 10,000 retained events including a truncation warning. If the limit is reached, successful inference still records incomplete telemetry scope, while timeout and cancellation outcomes retain their terminal state.

---

<!-- page:docs:security.md path:/docs/security -->
# Security and isolation

> Prepare the trusted runner, containers, credentials, and output boundary.


Treat repository files, issue text, test output, and model output as untrusted. The trusted boundary contains the installed CLI, base-revision policy, context collector, coordinator, and separate publisher. In CI, pass `--trusted-config-from-base` so a PR cannot change the policy or executable that evaluates itself.

Tests require a pinned Docker image with no network, no credentials, a read-only root, an unprivileged UID, and fixed CPU, memory, process, disk, and time limits. There is no host-execution fallback. PR inference requires the trusted `reviewfn-codex:0.154.0` image and an inference-only proxy; it must not receive a raw provider or GitHub publication token. Build that image from the packaged harness Dockerfile and provision the proxy before enabling reviews.

The review CLI refuses `GITHUB_TOKEN` in its environment. Put publication in a separate trusted job that reads a retained report and verifies the PR, head, and profile from event metadata. The CLI rejects changed auto-loaded agent instruction and configuration paths before inference. Locally trusted API-key and ChatGPT modes are not PR inference modes.

The [full security model](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/security.md) records exact bounds, redaction, artifact retention, symlink protection, platform caveats, and cleanup rules. Review it before running against untrusted code.

---

<!-- page:docs:workflow.md path:/docs/workflow -->
# Review workflow

> Follow exact revisions from context capture to validated report.


ReviewFn identifies the base, head, merge-base, diff, configuration, policy, prompt, harness, model, and budget for each run. It freezes authoritative issue and repository context before inference. A source adapter rejects a dirty review root, while the CLI clones committed input into its own checkout so mutable caller files are excluded.

Approved test commands are argv arrays, not shell scripts. The test adapter runs them in a bounded Docker container against a committed archive. The review harness receives the frozen evidence and returns structured assessments and findings. The validator checks source IDs, requirements, exact-head code anchors, test receipts, evidence links, severity, and verdict consistency before a report can be ready.

Every extracted requirement resolves to exactly one assessment. The report separates execution (`completed`, `failed`, and other states), coverage (`complete` or `incomplete`), and verdict (`ready`, `changes_requested`, or `needs_verification`). A completed model call alone does not imply a valid review. Once execution starts, missing context, malformed output, timeout, quota, cancellation, or stale-head outcomes remain visible in the report. Preflight failures such as unsupported authentication are returned as diagnostics and stop the run before a report is created.

Use the [report schema](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/report-schema.md) for field-level rules and [security model](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/security.md) for checkout, test, and inference isolation. To compare review quality, run [frozen evaluations](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/reference/evaluation.md) and retain their limitations.

---
